name: Week 26 KB Thursday — 🌀 B-Stance Flow Returns + the Press Tempo Structure
description:
**The press gets a structure instead of a bell.** 50 is the ceiling at this gym, so the only progression this lift has left is tempo — and rather than smearing three levers across every set, each set gets one job: **pause up, pause down, slow eccentric.** Your shape, and it's the right one.

**One amendment: the last set is capped by the DESCENT, not by failure.** Stop the set on the rep where the slow eccentric stops being slow. A slow eccentric taken to true failure means the final rep is a *failed* eccentric — maximum load at the exact moment position collapses, on an overhead lift, on the shoulder that flares.

**The B-Stance Flow comes back** after the Outside Snatch Flow's four-week run. It's conditioning, not the easy option.

dayOverview.theme: Thursday is the free slot — hard or experimental work here lands on Friday's legs day, which doesn't care about a tired arm, instead of Wednesday's pull day, which does. That's why the press tempo structure lives here and not on Tuesday. The opening flow rotates after four weeks of the same pairing: the B-Stance Flow comes back, and it is the conditioning option, not the light one.

spotlights.why: This is the lift the whole week's thinking has been about. 50 is the heaviest bell in the building, it read 'pretty easy' three weeks ago, and the lockout pause turned out to be a position audit rather than an intensity lever — feeling nothing during it means the stack is honest, which is a pass, not a failure. So the progression has to come from tempo, and the structure is one lever per set rather than all three at once. The thing to watch is not how hard it gets; it's whether the descent stays honest on the last set, because that's where the set actually ends.

The opening beat of a flow that has been off the sheet for two weeks, and the one that determines whether the rest of the chain works. A b-stance swing is a hinge with most of the load on one leg while the other only balances — which means the pelvis wants to rotate and the hips want to level out, and resisting that is the actual training effect. Get it wrong and it becomes a normal two-leg swing with a foot placed oddly; get it right and everything downstream in the flow inherits a stable single-leg hinge.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Thursday content rotates: W22 Outside Snatch + GymFiesta · W23-W25 Outside Snatch + Brutal Complex · W26 B-Stance Flow + Brutal Complex (current) · W27 candidates — the Outside Snatch Flow's return, the Dead Cluster Flow, or the GymFiesta circuit. The Brutal Complex holds the finisher slot for now; the opener is what cycles.
watchpoints: **🔆 PRESS TEMPO STRUCTURE — one lever per set, at 50, in this order** 🛑: **Set 1 — pause UP** (2-3s at lockout). **Set 2 — pause DOWN** (2-3s at the rack, on the way in). **Set 3 — slow eccentric**, 3-4s every rep.

**⚠️ Set 3 is capped by the DESCENT, not by failure. Stop the set on the rep where the eccentric stops taking 3-4 seconds.** That lands about a rep shy of failure, which is where an overhead 🛑 lift belongs.
**Handle DIAGONAL and deep in the hand** — base of the index finger to the heel of the hand. That's the forearm fix; some pressure at 50 is the implement, digging is position.
**🌀 B-Stance Flow returns — light bell, ladder 25 → 35.** b-stance swing → swing clean → ab-stance goblet squat → swing snatch → overhead lunge. **It's conditioning, not the easy option.**
**🔆 B-stance swing: the back foot is a kickstand, not a leg.** Keep the pelvis square — resisting the rotation is the point 🛑.
**🌀 Brutal Complex at 35 — rounds are the variable, not the bell.** You took four last week; four is the target now. **Stop a round when the hinge stops holding.**
**Bent press + windmill step to 40** 🛑. 35 was a non-event last week.
**KB row holds 50** — maintenance. **KB curl, LEFT FIRST**, light bell 🔥.
**Intensity tags:** 🔥 near-failure OK — KB curl, and the complex's round count. 🛑 keep it shy — overhead press, snatch, overhead lunge, bent press, windmill, the close-grip pushup.
**Banded shoulder prep + protective shrug stay in the warm-up.**
**Friday is legs.** If the complex leaves the QL tight, take the cool-down seriously.

sets.name: Warm-Up (incl. Bottoms-Up Cuff Prep + Figure-8 Passes)
sets.notes: Light bell throughout. The figure-8 passes here are the coordination primer — the heavy version lives on Tuesday.

exercises.notes: Slow, close to the head. Shoulders packed down.
Light bell inverted. Cuff prep and grip — and it rehearses the exact packed-down lockout the press block is about to ask for.
**Light bell** — coordination primer, not the 50lb Tuesday finisher. Hinge, don't squat.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked.
Protective activation. Down and back at the top.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~3 min)
sets.notes: 1 round of all 7 banded moves (~3 min). Sustained tension, no rest between positions.

sets.name: 🌀🔆 B-Stance Flow (@Asgooch) — Back On the Sheet
sets.notes:
**LADDER: 2 rounds per side at 25, then 2 at 35.** 5 reps each side per move, bell doesn't touch the ground within a round.

b-stance swing → swing clean → ab-stance goblet squat → swing snatch → overhead lunge.

**This is the conditioning option, not the easy one.** Every beat is unilateral or offset, so the trunk works the whole way through — it reads light on paper and doesn't run light.

**🔆 The b-stance swing sets up everything downstream:**
- **The back foot is a kickstand, not a leg.** Heel up, toe lightly down, and most of the load stays on the front leg
- **Keep the pelvis SQUARE.** The offset stance makes it want to rotate open; resisting that rotation is the actual training effect
- **It's a hinge, not a squat** — hips go back, bell to chest height off the hip snap, not the arm
- **Ribs down** through the whole swing

- **Swing clean: ride the momentum into the rack**, don't muscle it up — and let the bell land in the corner of the hand, not across the palm
- **Ab-stance goblet squat: stay in the offset stance** and squat anyway. That's the point
- **Swing snatch: punch the hand THROUGH** at the top, pack the shoulder down at lockout 🛑
- **Overhead lunge: arm locked, torso tall, ribs down.** The rib flare is the cheat

**Reflection:** on the b-stance swing, can you feel the front hip taking the load — or does it turn into a normal two-leg swing with a foot placed oddly?

sets.name: 🔆 Strength — Press Tempo Structure + KB Row + KB Curl 🛑
sets.notes:
3 rounds, run between the flow and the complex so the demanding volume isn't stacked at the top.

**The press runs a different lever on each of the three sets.** Row and curl stay the same across all three.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD: 50 across all three sets. Strict — clean to rack, press straight up, NO push-press.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — 50 is the ceiling bell here, so tempo is the whole progression. One lever per set:**

**SET 1 — PAUSE UP.** 2-3s at lockout on every rep. Bicep by the ear, shoulder packed DOWN, ribs down. Goes first while you're freshest — it needs the most force at the worst angle.

**SET 2 — PAUSE DOWN.** 2-3s on the way back into the rack, held at the hardest point of the descent rather than at the top.

**SET 3 — SLOW ECCENTRIC.** 3-4s down on every rep. **⚠️ CAPPED BY THE DESCENT, NOT BY FAILURE: stop the set on the rep where the eccentric stops taking 3-4 seconds.** A slow eccentric taken to true failure means the last rep is a *failed* eccentric — maximum load at the exact moment position collapses, overhead, on the shoulder that flares. The cue is the cap.

**Every set, regardless of lever:**
- **Strict, ribs DOWN**, no rib flare to get under it
- **Full lockout before any pause starts** — don't count from a soft elbow
- **Handle DIAGONAL in the hand** — base of the index finger to the heel of the hand, hand jammed deep into the corner of the handle. The bell then rests along the back of the forearm and the wrist neutralises on its own
- Both sides to the same standard

**On the forearm:** some pressure at 50 is the implement and always will be — the mass has to land somewhere. Digging and bruising is position.

**Reflection:** which of the three sets was actually hardest? And did the slow eccentric leave the arm noticeably tired afterwards — the way the ad-hoc version did three weeks ago?

**LOAD:** 50. Hinged, flat back, bell to the hip.
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN and BACK** before the elbow moves
- **Elbow drives past the ribs**, not flared wide
- Slow return, full stretch at the bottom

Maintenance — the real row volume lives on pull day.

**LOAD:** Light bell (~20-30lb). **LEFT ARM FIRST — match the right to it.**
- **Upper arm pinned to the ribs**, elbow doesn't drift forward
- **Slow lower to a FULL stretch** — the bell loads the bottom where a dumbbell goes slack
- **Shoulder packed DOWN**, no shrug to start

🔥 Near-failure fine on the last set. Twice a week is the dose — frequency for the left arm, not intensity.

sets.name: 🌀 Brutal Complex (@Asgooch) — 35, Four Rounds
sets.notes:
**LOAD: 35lb.** ~10-12 reps per move (each side where it alternates), circuit-style. Minimal rest between moves, ~60s between rounds.

swing → ab-stance goblet squat (alternate wide/narrow) → alternating bent-over row → close-grip pushup on the bell handles.

**Four rounds is the target** — you went past three under your own steam last week and called it 'so hard.' **Rounds stay the variable; the bell does not move.**

**Pace it by your own map:** the ab-stance squats and the close-grip pushups are the work; the swing and the row are the rest. Don't spend on the swings.

- **Close-grip pushup: hands on the bell handles, elbows TUCKED**, shoulders packed down, body in one line 🛑
- **Control the descent on the pushup** — the wobble is the training effect, and rushing throws it away
- **Stop a round when the hinge stops holding**, not when the clock says so. There's a bent-over row and loaded squats in here

**Reflection:** did round four hold its shape, or was it the round where the hinge started going?

sets.name: Skill — Bent Press + Windmill (40) 🛑
sets.notes:
2 rounds, unhurried. Skill practice at the end of a long day, not more work.

**Both step to 40** — 35 was a non-event last week, and 40 is the established working bell on the overhead leverage moves.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40lb.
- **A HINGE and a side bend, not a press** — the arm locks out and stays locked; the body moves underneath it
- **Eyes on the bell** the whole way down
- **Hips go BACK and to the side**; come up by driving the hips, not pressing the arm
- Shoulder packed DOWN throughout 🛑

**LOAD:** 40lb — heavy for a windmill, so keep the range honest.
- **Straight loaded arm, eyes on the bell**
- **Hinge to the opposite hip** — a hip hinge with rotation, not a side crunch
- **Long spine.** Back off the range before grinding it 🛑
- Slow and controlled both directions

sets.name: Cooldown (Hip + Adductor + QL Release)
sets.notes: Give the QL the full beat — the complex loaded the hinge hard and Friday is legs.

exercises.notes: Adductors — the ab-stance squats worked them.
30s each side. QL downshift, and Friday is legs.

tips: **One lever per set on the press.** Pause up, pause down, slow eccentric — and the last set ends when the descent stops being slow.
**Thursday is the free slot.** Hard or experimental work here lands on legs day, not pull day. If you want to mess with something, this is where.
**Left arm first on the curl.** Twice a week is the point.
